To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
transgenic tobacco plants expressing the 4-hydroxcinnamoyl-coenzyme A hydratase/ lyase (HCHl) gene from Agrobacterium tumefaciens have reduced lignin deposition and altered cell wall phenolics.
rerouting the phenolic pathway results in changes to the cell wall and vascular structure of tobacco stems.

rerouting the phenolic pathway by overexpression of HCHL results in reduced phenolic content and lignin biosynthesis, which in turn causes reduced stem toughness, distorted vasculature and coloration of the xylary tissues.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of metabolic rerouting of the phenylalanine pathway on cell wall and morphogenesis.
the impact of metabolic diversion in the phenylproponoid pathway and the resulting changes in the cell wall and morphogenetic processes.
the manipulation of the phenylalanine biosynthetic pathway and the effects of this on the cell wall and vascular system of plants.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
HCHL expression in tobacco causes cell wall and structural changes that may have a significant impact on plant growth and development.
the transgenic plants expressing HCHL exhibited altered cell wall phenolics, lignin deposition, vascular integrity and toughness.
HCHL expression in tobacco plants results in the diversion of the phenolic pathway, thereby causing a significant reduction in phenolics, lignin and toughness.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the phenylpropane shunt pathway is a viable approach for the production of novel phenolics and the manipulation of lignin and cell wall phenolics in transgenic tobacco.
the HCHL transgenic plants exhibited a range of cell wall and morphogenetic changes that were directly proportional to the expression of the HCHL gene.
transgenic tobacco plants expressing high levels of a bacterial HCHL gene exhibit reduced stem toughness concomitantly with a massive reduction and qualitative change in phenolics.
The main takeaway from our work is that
HCHL expression has a profound impact on vascular integrity and cell wall phenolic composition.
the phenylproponoid pathway is a highly integrated and tightly regulated network of metabolic pathways and the phenotypic consequences of modifying the pathway are not trivial.
metabolic rerouting can be used as a tool to modify plant cell wall phenolics and the vascular system.
